\subsection*{Simulation Platform: Simulation fidelity and its limits}
\noindent\textbf{6.}\quad \emph{table row:} \texttt{acc\_n} [m\,s$^{-2}/\sqrt{\mathrm{Hz}}$] \textbar{} \num{4.00e-3} \textbar{} \flag{\numrange{1.5e-2}{2.4e-2}} \textbar{} \num{2e-2} (\num{5.0}$\times$) \textbar{} \num{2.00e-3}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{7.}\quad \emph{table row:} \texttt{gyr\_w} [rad\,s$^{-2}/\sqrt{\mathrm{Hz}}$] \textbar{} \num{1.74e-6} \textbar{} not measurable \textbar{} \num{1e-4} (\flag{\num{58}$\times$}) \textbar{} --

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{8.\ \flag{[Threat to validity]}}\quad This is a bias with a known direction. The non-visual baselines of
\reportref{sec:results-proprio} run on a floor where the wheels effectively cannot
slip and with an encoder of unlimited resolution, which is dead reckoning's
best case. Both idealizations favour the proprioceptive estimators over the
visual ones, and neither has been relaxed, so any conclusion that a
wheel-plus-IMU filter matches the visual pipelines holds \emph{under these
conditions}, not in general.

\medskip

\section*{Chapter 4 --- Experiments and Results}

\subsection*{Experiment 1: Estimator Comparison Against a Non-Visual Baseline: Simulation}
\noindent\textbf{1.}\quad \slotstatus{completed}{Four \repo{dataset_allsensor_realistic} recordings, two
layouts each recorded without and with warehouse traffic. Two families of
estimator are scored over the full common interval of each: the non-visual
ones --- wheel odometry, IMU dead reckoning, an EKF at the visual systems' own
inertial noise configuration and a measured-noise EKF as diagnostic --- and
the visual ones, VINS-Fusion once per recording and ORB-SLAM3 with a CPU or
GPU feature extractor and its loop closer active or disabled. Traffic is noted
as a condition, not tested as a factor. The latency and resource measurement
is taken from eighteen repeated runs on the two mapping recordings, three
repeats of each of six configurations, and those repeats are the only
within-configuration spread the campaign measures.}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{2.}\quad \flag{Those two clean values are not themselves as low
as the stable runs', which span \SIrange{0.016}{0.037}{\metre}.} Which front-end condition produces them is not isolated here; the CPU runs of
the same recordings are scored below, where the same pattern recurs.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{3.}\quad \flag{One run per cell, and ORB-SLAM3's spread
  over identical repeats reaches \SI{0.277}{\metre} on these recordings ---
  wider than five of the eight gaps in (b) --- so no individual line is
  evidence. What the figure supports is the contrast between the panels: a
  shift every pair agrees on against one they do not.}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{4.}\quad The episodes are places, the untextured perimeter wall, and
its one excursion on \repo{realistic_002} (\SI{0.05}{} to \SI{0.61}{\metre}
between \SI{17}{} and \SI{24}{\second}) is one of them, reproduced by a second
run to within \SI{6}{\milli\metre} (\reportref{fig:exp1-vins-starvation}). \flag{The low-feature seconds are \SIrange{8}{20}{\percent} of each run and
carry \SIrange{10}{20}{\percent} of its positive error growth: their median
rate is higher, but most of the growth accrues over the many seconds at the
ceiling, so they cause VINS-Fusion's excursions and not its ATE.} ORB-SLAM3 passes the same wall in under a second
on its inertial prediction, with no step.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{5.}\quad \flag{One
  repeat on one recording: it establishes that the excursion belongs to the
  recording and not to the run, and no more.}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{6.}\quad \flag{The hypothesis
this project is named for is therefore supported in one configuration, a
vehicle leading the robot, as a strong local and small accumulated effect over
four seconds of a 117-second recording; ``movers degrade the estimate'' as a
general statement is not what these recordings show.}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{7.}\quad The jack had been in view, moving, for the nine seconds
  before the band --- \SIrange{6}{20}{\metre} away and small in the image ---
  with no effect; the cost begins when it is close enough to fill the view. \flag{One episode on one recording: it shows what happens when a
  vehicle leads the robot and how large the effect is, not how often a
  warehouse puts the robot in that situation.}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{8.}\quad \flag{Excitation is confounded with layout, two routes
against two routes, and on \repo{realistic_001} a comparable tilt does not
convert into drift ($r = \num{-0.49}$), so the mechanism is shown on one
recording, not established.} Scale is not a factor: ORB-SLAM3's
\SIrange{1.7}{5.4}{\percent} path excess is the pre-initialization spike and
frame jitter, and its local scale over each second is
\numrange{0.997}{0.999}.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{9.}\quad \flag{Three repeats per configuration on one laptop,
  not interleaved, so the bars measure repeatability inside a session and not
  the thermal state between sessions.}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{10.\ \flag{[Confound: run order]}}\quad The GPU and CPU repeats were made in
separate sessions on a laptop that throttles at \SI{90}{\celsius}, and on the
I recording the GPU front end's advantage reverses (\SI{52}{} against
\SI{44}{\milli\second}, \SI{75}{} against \SI{91}{\percent} of frames kept).
The U-recording figures are the ones to quote until the runs are repeated
interleaved from a cool start.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{11.\ \flag{[Open: the false closure is diagnosed, not fixed]}}\quad Both front ends accept the same false closure on \repo{realistic_001}, and the
matched pair is the same repeated asset from opposite sides of the building
(\reportref{fig:exp1-false-closure}). The guards that would catch it, a
covisibility-consistency window or a maximum correction against the inertial
drift bound, are untested.

\medskip

\subsection*{Experiment 1: Estimator Comparison Against a Non-Visual Baseline: Real robot}
\noindent\textbf{12.}\quad \slotstatus{partial}{Four real recordings with an independent planar reference
(\repo{dataset_realv6_000}, \repo{dataset_realv7_000} to \repo{_002}).
ORB-SLAM3 tracks every recording in four configurations at
\SIrange{0.19}{0.48}{\metre} planar ATE, the configurations of a \repo{realv7}
recording agreeing to \SI{0.02}{\metre}. Wheel+gyro dead reckoning, with one speed
constant fitted on \repo{realv7_000} and held, is in the same accuracy class.
VINS-Fusion completes every recording at \SIrange{0.37}{0.79}{\metre} once the
fisheye field of view is masked at \SI{70}{\degree} and the stereo extrinsic
frozen. The EKF cannot be formed, because the rig publishes no steering
measurement. Every accuracy value is provisional until the marker-to-IMU lever
arm is measured.}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{13.}\quad \flag{Every estimator on every \repo{realv7} run sits
\SIrange{0.2}{0.4}{\metre} ahead of the tracker marker along the direction of
travel while the wheel+gyro baseline, aligned with the same offset, does not;
a diagnostic lever-arm fit would take the ORB-SLAM3 figures to
\SIrange{0.12}{0.21}{\metre}. It is not used: measuring the arm on the rig is
the largest remaining correction to every real-robot figure.}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{14.}\quad The simulation's
memory trade does not transfer: on the robot VINS-Fusion holds
\SIrange{1.05}{1.09}{\gibi\byte} against ORB-SLAM3's
\SIrange{1.13}{1.44}{\gibi\byte} while still using more cores. \flag{One of six loop-closing repeats on \repo{realv6} accepted a single
closure with a \SI{36.4}{\metre} correction and finished \SI{10.7}{\metre}
off: no loop-closing figure on the robot is safe from the closer.}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{15.}\quad \flag{One run per cell. What the figure supports is the
  pattern across the six pairs, not any single line.}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{16.}\quad \flag{The real ATE carries the unmeasured lever arm;
the RPE carries it only through turns, since a body-fixed offset cancels in a
displacement along a straight segment.}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{17.}\quad \flag{One run per
  configuration per recording on the real side; the comparison is between the
  medians of two populations and not a paired test, so it supports the size of
  the difference and not a per-configuration one.}

\medskip

\subsection*{Experiment 2: Visual-Inertial Odometry on a Prior Map: Simulation}
\noindent\textbf{18.}\quad \slotstatus{partial}{The tiny-warehouse map passes every map target. The two
realistic-warehouse maps that part~B relocalizes on fail them, although their
poses are accurate: the failure is in how the occupancy grid is built. The
tiny map's independent drivability reference is lost, and the large-warehouse
attempt is unauditable.}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{19.}\quad \flag{The independent route is lost, so the
drivability half is a dated measurement, and that route was one loop of a wide
aisle, so \SI{0.7}{\percent} is a floor, not a worst case.}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{20.}\quad Both are inside the
\SI{0.25}{\metre} tolerance at which the grids were scored, so a grid built from
perfect poses would have been scored the same way: the precision and
false-obstacle losses are produced where the grid is built from the depth image
--- the sensor range, the ground-height threshold and the ray tracing of
\reportref{sec:map-eval-method} --- and that is where a fix has to be looked for. \flag{The I-layout graph reaches \SI{2.59}{\metre} at its worst node against
\SI{0.29}{\metre} on the U layout, a local excursion the rms hides; and a graph
is scored at its nodes, one every few metres, so a pose error that appears and
is corrected between two nodes is not seen here.}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{21.}\quad \slotstatus{partial}{Six live runs of 15 November 2026, in the two static
worlds, measure the localization against ground truth over hand-driven routes
of \SIrange{21}{148}{\metre}. Neither traffic world is measured, so
nothing here speaks to a dynamic warehouse. No goal was commanded in any of the
six either, so the goal-reaching measures of the reporting rules below are
still unused and that half of the experiment remains \status{planned}. The protocol, goal set and
success criteria are fixed before the first run.}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{22.}\quad \paragraph{Reporting rules, goal-reaching.} \flag{Fixed before any run exists,
so that the result cannot be chosen after the fact, and left unchanged here.} A
goal counts as reached when the base frame is within \SI{1.0}{\metre} and
\SI{30}{\degree} of it and the planner reports success.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{23.}\quad \paragraph{Reporting rules, pose tracking.} \flag{Defined after these data
existed, and reported as the weaker claim it is.} Error is the planar distance
between the published \texttt{map}~$\rightarrow$~\texttt{base\_link} transform,
sampled at \SI{2}{\hertz}, and the ground truth interpolated to the same
instants, with no lever arm (see Frames).

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{24.}\quad \flag{One configuration throughout.} The slot reports the correction gate
enabled with a position threshold of
\SI{1.5}{\metre}, recorded on 15 November 2026.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{25.}\quad The gate refuses a correction
larger than the front end's own drift since the last accepted fix, which is
what stops a repeated rack face being matched at the wrong aisle. \flag{The \texttt{rep} index in the recording directories is a configuration
index and not a repeat index, so none of these runs are replicates of one
another and nothing here measures run-to-run spread.}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{26.}\quad \flag{Splitting the panels exposes a pattern the single axis hid.} All six
runs begin within \SIrange{0.108}{0.137}{\metre} of truth, but every
I-layout run then climbs to five to eleven times that before a fix pulls it
back --- \SI{0.519}{}, \SI{0.765}{} and \SI{1.229}{\metre}, each peaking
between \SI{19.5}{} and \SI{23.0}{\metre} driven --- where no U-layout run
exceeds twice its starting error.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{27.}\quad \flag{That bias is not uniform, and the reason is where it enters.} Only the
I-layout straight is genuinely one-signed, with every sample negative; the
figure-of-eight is negative in \SI{75}{\percent} of its samples and the square
in \SI{56}{\percent}, crossing zero repeatedly.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{28.}\quad \flag{It does not follow
that the word count is uninformative.} Among the rejections the zero-support and some-support groups
do differ in word count --- medians of \num{56} and \num{106} --- but their
ranges overlap across \numrange{24}{165}, and the rank correlation of
\num{0.24} is measured only where the inlier count is already truncated to
\numrange{0}{19} of the \num{20} needed, which attenuates it by construction.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{29.}\quad \flag{This is a replay of logged corrections, not a run with the gate switched
off.} A robot steered by Nav2 on a wrong pose would have driven differently; these routes were
hand-driven, so the path is the same either way.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{30.}\quad Planar error rises with the ground-truth yaw rate
in all six runs ($\rho$ \numrange{0.09}{0.76}, sign test $p = \num{0.031}$). \flag{It cannot be attributed to turning.} Yaw rate and speed are confounded in
every run ($\rho$ \numrange{0.34}{0.91}), so the measurement cannot separate
turning from simply moving, and part of the effect is the timebase recorded
below.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{31.}\quad \flag{Some of the reported error is timebase, and the slot cannot say how
much.} Fitting a constant time offset between each estimate and the ground
truth returns offsets of \emph{opposite sign}: the published pose matches best
when shifted by between \SI{-0.04}{\second} and \SI{-0.12}{\second}, the front end's own trajectory
when shifted \SIrange{+0.20}{+0.26}{\second}, on the same runs against the same
truth.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{32.}\quad \paragraph{Insight: over these distances the prior supplies a datum, not
accuracy.} \flag{This narrows the objective stated above, and is the claim the
data support.} Unaided ORB-SLAM3, rigidly aligned onto ground truth, drifts by a
median of \SIrange{0.013}{0.307}{\metre} over these \SIrange{21}{148}{\metre}
routes, never exceeds \SI{0.64}{\metre} at any instant, and ends each run
between \SI{0.02}{\metre} and \SI{0.42}{\metre} from truth.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{33.}\quad \flag{The ordering is suggestive and is not a measurement.} Six runs, one per
cell, on hand-driven routes that differ in shape as well as length, so route
length is confounded with layout and with everything else that differs between
cells.

\medskip

\subsection*{Experiment 2: Visual-Inertial Odometry on a Prior Map: Real robot}
\noindent\textbf{34.}\quad \slotstatus{planned}{No RTAB-Map database has been built from real imagery, no
reference geometry of the site exists to score one against, and so no
relocalization on the real robot can be scored either.}
